definition: fastai is a high-level deep learning library on PyTorch that trains state-of-the-art vision, text and tabular models in a few lines.
details: Created by Jeremy Howard and Sylvain Gugger at fast.ai (2018), alongside the free Practical Deep Learning course.

explainer.lead: How to install fastai, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from fastai.vision.all import *

path = untar_data(URLs.PETS) / "images"
dls = ImageDataLoaders.from_name_func(
    path, get_image_files(path), valid_pct=0.2,
    label_func=lambda f: f.name[0].isupper(), item_tfms=Resize(224))
learn = vision_learner(dls, resnet34, metrics=error_rate)
learn.fine_tune(1)

explainer.inAi: Great for learning and for fast transfer-learning baselines on your own images or text.
explainer.jsNote: fastai is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is like a ready-made kitchen with the knives sharpened, so you can cook a good meal without assembling every tool first.
tiers.practitioner: Teams use its high-level APIs for quick baselines and standard training recipes; the pitfall is that unusual architectures or custom training loops may need dropping to plain PyTorch.
tiers.paperLevel: A high-level deep learning library layered on PyTorch covering vision, text and tabular models; created by Jeremy Howard and Sylvain Gugger at fast.ai in 2018. Limits: abstractions can constrain nonstandard custom training.

explainer.example: A few lines load an image dataset and train a fine-tuned vision model to competitive accuracy.
